title: Grill: New Task panel and Git launch dialogs redesign
summary:
There is no spec for this redesign, so this record becomes the contract. It holds **16 decisions** plus a **confirm-or-override list** of 8 defaults.

Start with **Scope & architecture**, because those answers decide how big the plan is: which surfaces change, and whether the panel moves onto the dialogs' shared launch picker. **Layout** and **Visual language** decide what it looks like. **Bugs, copy, process** settles the rest.

The brief is `docs/plans/new-task-ui-ux-investigation.md`. Baseline screenshots of today's panel and issue dialog are in the investigation step's scratchpad. Your progress is saved in the browser as you go.

proven.text: **Two launch-picker implementations have drifted apart. This is the main cause of "no clear pattern".** The panel keeps its own harness/mode/model/effort/speed state and markup (`NewTaskForm.tsx:917-1247`). Every dialog (issue, PR conflicts, Clone, Settings → Agents) uses `TaskLaunchPickers`. They differ in the Mode control, model refresh, the status dot, the hint position, the remembered picks, the pipeline preflight and the Manage agents row.
**Bug: the panel submits Speed = Off for claude-code and codex even when Fast is picked.** The gate predates wave 4, and no e2e catches it.

**Bug: every issue with an author shows a false warning in the issue dialog**: "`@<author>` doesn't match a project file". The issue prompt names people as `@login` (`src/shared/issue-task.ts:286`, `:439`), and the composer's warning doesn't exclude handles.

proven: **Visual audit.** There are 5 control heights and 2 type sizes in one column, and 4 kinds of dropdown (native select, SearchSelect, the Agent/Pipeline popover, the Extension picker). The selected chips use the solid primary-button style, so they look like the Run button. Isolate is a native checkbox while Max Mode is a Switch. No label is associated with its control. Helper text uses fixed `text-[11px]`/`text-[10px]` sizes that don't follow Cmd+/−. There are no sections. Names truncate at `w-80`. The dialog chrome is hand-copied in each dialog.
**It's a webview-only change.** It needs no route, migration or server change. The create payload stays the same apart from the Speed fix. Light and dark themes must both work (repo rule).

**Hand-written primitives.** The repo has no Radix and uses Tailwind v3. New primitives (Field/Label, Checkbox or Switch, segmented control, dialog parts) are hand-written in shadcn's shape, not added with `bunx shadcn add`. Every popover inside a dialog keeps the `data-popover-open` Escape contract.

**Earlier owner decisions still stand.** From the Select Projects grill: one combined control, read-only Branch rows that reopen the dialog, one shared Branch name, the most recent project auto-selected, and the selection kept after submit. **One selection** across Pipeline, Agent and manual harness. **No remembered last-used** agent or pipeline.

sections.title: Scope & architecture
sections.intro: These decide how big the plan is and which files it owns.

questions.title: Which surfaces adopt the new pattern in this change?
questions.why: Decides the file set, the e2e specs to update, and whether a 'legacy' variant is needed anywhere.
questions.context: The panel and the two Git dialogs are in by definition. The others share components with them. **Clone → "Explain this repository"** and **Settings → Agents** render `TaskLaunchPickers`, so they change automatically if it's restyled. **RunPanel's send box** renders `PromptComposer` (`RunPanel.tsx:4985`), so a change to the composer's label row, references strip or warning shows up there too, unless it's gated behind a variant. **Select projects** and **Branch naming** are opened from the panel and from the issue dialog.

options.label: Select projects dialog
options.consequence: Adopts the new dialog parts and controls; `select-projects.spec.ts` and `multi-repo-task.spec.ts` locators are updated.

options.label: Branch naming dialog (the gear on Branch name)
options.consequence: Small; it adopts the dialog parts and Field.

options.label: Clone → "Explain this repository"
options.consequence: Gets the new launch picker for free; `clone-project.spec.ts` is updated.

options.label: Settings → Agents (agent profile form)
options.consequence: Gets the new launch picker (it hides the profile picker); `agent-profiles*` specs are updated.

options.label: RunPanel send box: shared-primitive changes only
options.description: The send box picks up the new tokens, text sizes and label association through PromptComposer, but its layout doesn't change.
options.consequence: Small regression risk; a send-box screenshot is added to acceptance.

options.label: RunPanel send box: full redesign too
options.consequence: A big extra surface (it has many layout slots); probably a separate ticket.

recommendation.reason: Every surface that starts a task reads as one pattern. The send box gets only the shared fixes, so this doesn't turn into a RunPanel redesign.

questions.title: Should the panel move onto one shared launch-picker component that every dialog uses too?
questions.why: This ends the drift for good, and about 450 lines of `NewTaskForm` launch state move into `useTaskLaunch`.
questions.context: `NewTaskForm` has its own copy: `agentCache`, seed effects, `switchAgent`, and duplicated JSX at `:917-1247`. Its hidden behaviors would have to move with it, each with a test first: the per-kind cache, pending seeds for catalog-only models, the `modelTouched` guard, the stale profile/pipeline guards, `effectiveStatus` vs `selectedStatus`, and the gemini overage check on the pipeline's start step.

options.label: One shared component (useTaskLaunch + TaskLaunchPickers, redesigned) used by the panel and every dialog
options.consequence: The biggest refactor, but one place to style, one set of tests and no future drift.

options.label: Keep two implementations and restyle both to match
options.consequence: Less churn now, but the drift comes back with the next harness feature.

options.label: Redesign the panel only and leave the dialogs' picker as it is
options.consequence: The panel and the dialogs still look different, which contradicts the goal.

recommendation.reason: The drift is the root cause, and the dialogs already prove the shared module works across five consumers.

questions.title: Which of the panel-only or dialog-only behaviors should every surface get?
questions.why: Each selected item becomes shared behavior with a test. An unselected item is dropped wherever it exists today.
questions.context: Each option is a behavior that exists on only one side today. The **Mode control** gets its own question below.

options.label: Model refresh ↻ (panel only today)
Three-state status dot: green / amber when logged out / red (dialogs only)
Harness tooltip with account email + today's token burn (panel only)
Unavailable / not-logged-in hint right under the harness picker (dialogs), not at the end of the block (panel)
Fable / Mythos "2x usage" notes (panel only)
Switching harness restores that harness's previous picks (panel); the dialogs reset to defaults
Remember Speed and Max Mode per harness (panel only)
Pipeline runnability preflight that blocks Run with a reason (dialogs only)
Pipeline loading/error/empty hints (dialogs only)
"Manage agents…" row in the Agent picker (panel only)
Disable **Run task** in the panel when the harness is unavailable; **To backlog** stays enabled (behavior change)
options.consequence: Matches the dialogs' gating. Today the panel lets you click Run, and the start then fails.

recommendation.reason: Each one is the richer or safer side. Taking them all keeps every feature and ends the drift.

questions.title: How should Mode be picked?
questions.why: Today the panel shows two controls for one value: Code/Plan pills plus a select, where picking Plan in the select also flips the pills. The dialogs show a single native select with no hints.

options.label: A Code | Plan segmented control. Under Code, a compact variant picker (Auto / Accept edits / Ask…) with hints, shown only when the harness has more than one Code variant
options.consequence: One value, one obvious control, and plan is one click. The per-harness Plan tooltips stay.

options.label: One Mode picker with hints that lists every mode, Plan included
options.consequence: The simplest option; Plan is two clicks away.

options.label: Keep today's panel version (pills + select) everywhere

recommendation.reason: It keeps the one-click Code/Plan the panel has today and removes the redundant second control under Plan.

questions.title: How should the roughly 16 controls be organised?
questions.why: Decides the panel's skeleton, the dialogs' skeleton, and how much e2e churn there is.
questions.context: Today it's one flat `space-y-3` column. The header InfoTip explains three groups (what / where / who) that the layout never shows. Form guidance (NN/g, Smashing) says to group into labelled sections and to put rarely changed settings behind progressive disclosure. **Every feature stays reachable either way.**

options.label: Three labelled sections (**Task** · **Workspace** · **Agent**). Workspace and Agent can collapse to a one-line summary that expands on click; the state is remembered in localStorage
options.preview:
TASK
  Type  [Task|Bug|Spike]
  Title / Prompt / Files
WORKSPACE  agetor · fix/7c5261 · isolated   ▸
AGENT      Claude Code · Opus 5.5 · High · Code ▸
options.consequence: Shortest panel. Your usual settings show at a glance and you can change them in one click.

options.label: Three labelled sections, always expanded
options.consequence: Clearer grouping, but the same length as today.

options.label: Sections plus one "Advanced" disclosure (branch name, model/effort/speed, max mode)
options.consequence: Hides settings you may change often; see the next question.

options.label: Keep the flat column with better spacing and dividers

recommendation.reason: It shows the what/where/who model the InfoTip already explains and shortens the panel without hiding anything behind an unlabeled 'Advanced'.

questions.title: Which fields do you change on most tasks (more than half)?
questions.why: Fields you change often stay visible. The others can live in a collapsed summary line.

options.label: Type (Task/Bug/Spike)
Title
Prompt
Files / Folders
MCP · Skills · Plugins · Agents · Prompts
Project(s)
Isolate
Branch name
Pipeline
Agent (profile)
Harness / account
Mode (Code/Plan)
Model
Effort
Speed / Max Mode

recommendation.reason: A guess from the screenshots, which show many accounts and pipelines. Please correct it; only you know your habits.

questions.title: How should a harness be picked when there are 7 or more accounts?
questions.why: Your 4 Claude accounts differ mainly in the suffix that the 2-column grid truncates ("Claude PBS…", "Claude …").
questions.context: Today it's a 2-column button grid with an icon, the name, a stack chip (`1/2`) and a status dot. The Agent and Pipeline pickers are already custom popovers with icon rows.

options.label: A searchable picker in the same style as Agent and Pipeline (rows: icon, full name, stack chip, status dot, account email), with the current choice shown in the trigger
options.consequence: One dropdown family for Agent, Pipeline and Harness. It scales to any number of accounts. Picking takes 2 clicks, not 1.

options.label: A one-column list of full-width rows (always visible)
options.consequence: No truncation and 1 click, but 7+ rows of height.

options.label: Keep the 2-column grid and widen the panel
options.consequence: Still truncates as accounts grow.

recommendation.reason: It scales, ends the truncation, and makes Harness consistent with Agent and Pipeline, the pickers it shares its one-selection rule with.

questions.title: How wide should the New Task panel be?
questions.why: Today it's a fixed `w-80` (320 px), which truncates branch names, project rows and the Extensions trigger.

options.label: Resizable with a drag handle, default 384 px, min 320, max 560, the width remembered in localStorage (like the collapse state)
options.consequence: A new handle and one localStorage key; the board gives up the space.

options.label: Fixed 384 px (`w-96`)
Keep 320 px

recommendation.reason: It fixes truncation for long names without forcing the extra width on a small laptop screen.

questions.title: How should the issue and PR-conflict dialogs be laid out?
questions.why: The issue dialog today is one `max-w-lg` column that repeats the whole panel: a long scroll at 85vh.

options.label: A wider two-column dialog (about `max-w-4xl`): issue context, Type, Prompt and Files on the left; Workspace and Agent sections on the right; a sticky footer. One column below about 768 px
options.consequence: No long scroll, and the prompt gets room. The same sections as the panel, laid out side by side.

options.label: Keep one column, using the same sections and collapsible summaries as the panel
options.consequence: Shorter than today, but the prompt and settings still compete for height.

options.label: Keep today's single column (restyle only)

recommendation.reason: The dialog has the room the sidebar lacks. Two columns put the issue text next to the settings it informs.

questions.title: How should a selected toggle (Type, Mode, a harness) look?
questions.why: Today selected chips use the solid primary-button style (white in dark mode). They're the brightest thing on the panel and compete with the Run task button.

options.label: Subtle: an accent background, a primary-colored ring/border and normal text; solid primary is reserved for the main action
options.consequence: One clear CTA. It must be checked in both themes.

options.label: Keep solid primary for the selected state

recommendation.reason: Standard segmented-control practice: the selected state shouldn't look like a button to press.

questions.title: Should Model, Effort and Mode-variant use the same custom picker as Agent, Pipeline and Harness, or stay native `<select>`?
questions.why: There are four dropdown kinds today. One family means one trigger style, one popover style and one keyboard behavior.
questions.context: Native selects are simple and accessible, but they can't show hints, icons or a disabled reason, and they look different from the custom popovers next to them. 7 e2e specs reach Model and Effort through native-select XPath. Those break either way once the fields move into sections.

options.label: One custom picker family (built from `SearchSelect`) for every dropdown in these surfaces
options.consequence: Consistent look and hints. The e2e specs move to stable test ids. The `data-popover-open` contract is applied to each one.

options.label: Native select for short lists (Model, Effort, variant) and custom pickers only where rows need icons

recommendation.reason: Consistency is the goal, and Model rows benefit from hints such as the 2x-usage note or 'not in this CLI'.

questions.title: Which issues found along the way get fixed in this change?

options.label: Fast speed dropped for claude-code/codex on New Task submit (`NewTaskForm.tsx:724`), plus a form-submit e2e that pins it
False `@author` warning in the issue dialog
The stale `TaskLaunchPickers` header comment ("refactored onto this module in a later change")

recommendation.reason: All are small, and the redesign touches each of these lines anyway. Leaving a known bug in a file you rewrite would leave the change unfinished.

questions.title: How should the false `@author` warning be fixed?
questions.context: The handles come from `src/shared/issue-task.ts:286` and `:439`. `agetor add --issue` shares that builder, so changing the prompt text changes the CLI's prompt too.

options.label: The composer's warning ignores `@tokens` that don't look like paths (no `/`, no `.`, matches a GitHub login pattern)
options.consequence: Fixes it for typed prompts as well; prompt text unchanged.

options.label: Write author names without `@` in the issue prompt
options.consequence: Changes the prompt that both the CLI and the UI send.

options.label: Suppress the warning for text seeded from the issue and keep it for what the user types

recommendation.reason: It leaves the prompt the agent sees (and the CLI parity) unchanged and fixes the false positive at its source.

questions.title: What should the actions be called, the same in every surface?
questions.why: Today the panel says "To backlog" / "Run task", and the dialogs say "Cancel" / "Create & start" for the same create-and-start action.

options.label: Primary **Run task** everywhere. Panel secondary: **Add to backlog**. Dialogs: **Cancel** + **Run task**
options.consequence: One verb everywhere. e2e names that change: "Create & start" and "To backlog".

options.label: Same, and the dialogs also get **Add to backlog** (creates the task without starting it)
options.consequence: A small new capability for the dialogs.

options.label: Keep today's labels

recommendation.reason: One vocabulary without adding scope. Pick the second option if you want to queue issues without starting them.

questions.title: Three peer branches are also redesigning UI (App bar, TaskCard, the file chip). Who owns the new shared primitives and tokens?
questions.why: All four branches may touch `ui/*`, `index.css`/`tailwind.config.js` tokens, `StackPositionChip` and `AgentIcon`, so expect merge conflicts.
questions.context: The investigation messaged those peers (no reply). The likely new primitives here: Field/Label, a Checkbox or Switch for Isolate, a SegmentedControl, Dialog Header/Body/Footer, rem-based small-text tokens.

options.label: This branch adds them additively (new files and new tokens only, no edits to existing primitives' defaults) and announces them to the peers
options.consequence: Few conflicts; peers can adopt them later.

options.label: A small primitives-only PR merges first, and all four branches build on it
options.consequence: The cleanest, but it blocks on a fifth change.

options.label: Keep the new pieces local to the New Task components

recommendation.reason: It unblocks this work without editing what the peers are editing.

questions.title: What does done mean?

options.label: Before/after screenshots of every in-scope surface in **both themes**, attached to the PR
A committed component and style spec (sections, control sizes, spacing, selected/disabled/error states, which picker for what) under `docs/architecture/`
Accessibility: every control has an associated label, the whole form works by keyboard (Tab order, Escape contract), focus is visible, AA contrast in both themes
The full e2e suite is green after locator migration, plus new e2e for the form-submit Speed, Cmd+Enter and section collapse
A RunPanel send-box screenshot proving no layout regression

recommendation.reason: A style spec is what keeps the next change from re-creating the drift. Screenshots and a11y prove the result.

sections.title: Confirm or override
sections.intro: Defaults I'd bet on. One click each.

questions.title: Control size standard

recommendation.value: One size for every field and toggle in these surfaces: `h-9`, `text-sm` (the primitives' default), with no per-site overrides.
recommendation.reason: Ends the 5 heights. Sections and the wider panel absorb the extra height.

questions.title: Small text sizes

recommendation.value: Add rem-based tokens (`text-2xs` = 0.6875rem, `text-3xs` = 0.625rem) in `tailwind.config.js` and use them in the in-scope files, so helper text follows Cmd+/−. The other ~490 app-wide `text-[11px]` uses are **out of scope** (a separate sweep).
recommendation.reason: Fixes these surfaces now without an app-wide diff.

questions.title: Isolate control

recommendation.value: Replace the native checkbox with the hand-rolled `Switch` (as Max Mode uses), label associated, `data-testid="isolate-toggle"` kept.
recommendation.reason: One boolean control everywhere; no blue OS checkbox.

questions.title: Dialog parts

recommendation.value: Add `DialogHeader` / `DialogTitle` / `DialogDescription` / `DialogBody` / `DialogFooter` to `ui/dialog.tsx` and adopt them in the in-scope dialogs. Other dialogs adopt them later, when touched.
recommendation.reason: Removes the copy-pasted chrome without editing unrelated dialogs.

questions.title: Keyboard submit

recommendation.value: Cmd/Ctrl+Enter triggers **Run task** in the panel and the dialogs (shown as a hint on the button). It is inert while a popover or autocomplete is open, and it does nothing when Run is disabled.
recommendation.reason: Common practice, and there is no shortcut today. Backlog stays a click.

questions.title: Panel header CLI version

recommendation.value: Remove the raw CLI `--version` text from the panel header; the version stays in the harness picker's row tooltip.
recommendation.reason: It adds noise and reads "--version" with stub binaries.

questions.title: e2e locator churn

recommendation.value: Update the ~15 affected specs in the same change. Move DOM-path XPath locators (Model/Effort/Mode) to stable test ids (`new-task-*` / `launch-*` unify to one prefix, e.g. `launch-model-picker`). Keep the accessible names that the e2e asserts unless a decision above renames them.
recommendation.reason: Today's anchors can't survive sections; test ids stop the next redesign from breaking them again.

questions.title: Panel form factor

recommendation.value: The panel stays a left sidebar: always mounted, collapsible to its rail, an aside-wide drop zone, the onboarding spotlight target. The Branch summary row becomes a visibly clickable row, and "Reset to pattern" and "Change" become small ghost buttons.
recommendation.reason: Keeps the collapse, onboarding and drop-zone contracts, and fixes the low-affordance controls.
